sections.h2: Who bills Lee County property tax, and who sets the value?
sections.html:
Two separate Lee County offices handle your property tax: the Property Appraiser sets the value and keeps exemptions, and the Tax Collector mails the bill and takes payment. If your question is about value, exemptions or a mailing address, call the appraiser at 239-533-6100; if it is about paying, call the Tax Collector at 239-533-6000.

The split matters when you sell a Lee County house. The Tax Collector says plainly that it cannot change values or exemptions, and the appraiser cannot take a payment. Questions about a special assessment for roads, fire, water or sewer go to the authority that levied it, whose contact details sit on the tax bill itself.

  • Lee County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, parcel records, mailing address changes.
  • Lee County Tax Collector: bills, payments, installment and partial payment plans, homestead deferral.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: records the deed, collects document stamp tax, and hosts the Value Adjustment Board paperwork.

sections.h2: When is Lee County property tax due, and what does paying early save?
sections.html:
Lee County real estate tax becomes payable November 1 and is due in full by March 31 of the following year. Anything still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent under Florida law.

Florida prints an early-payment discount scale of 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. The Lee Tax Collector confirms the November discount applies even when a former mortgage lender is still listed on the notice. A bill paid in March carries no discount.

Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach all sit inside this one county billing cycle, so a seller in any of them gets the same dates. The Tax Collector accepts payment online, by phone, by mail, in person, and through drop-off lockers at four service centers. Delinquent real estate tax cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck, which is worth knowing before a closing deadline.

sections.h2: What payment plans does the Lee County Tax Collector offer?
sections.html:
Lee County offers three: a quarterly installment plan, a partial payment plan, and a homestead tax deferral. Each has its own deadline, and the installment plan has the earliest.

Lee County Tax Collector plans, from the office's payment options page
PlanApplyKey rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

The installment discounts run 6 percent on the first payment, 4.5 percent on the second and 3 percent on the third, with none on the fourth. Miss the first payment by July 31 and the account drops out of the plan. Partial payments are open only for the current year and are not available for delinquent tax. A person on the installment plan cannot also use the partial plan.

If a house sells after one or more installments are paid, the new owner has to continue the plan for that tax year. Tell the buyer's closing agent about it early.

sections.h2: How do homestead and senior exemptions work in Lee County?
sections.html:
Homestead takes the first $25,000 of assessed value off every tax, plus an additional amount that applies only to non-school taxes. For tax year 2026 the Lee appraiser prints the additional amount as up to $26,411, and it applies to assessed value above $50,000.

File Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1, online at leepa.org, by email to exemptions@leepa.org, by mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or in person at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The office says all applications are processed by July 1. Once homestead is granted, the Save Our Homes limit on yearly assessment growth follows the year after.

Lee County jurisdictions set their own senior exemption amounts for owners 65 and older within the income limit:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veterans, disabled first responders, surviving spouses, deployed service members, and $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew each January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

sections.h2: What happens to a homestead exemption when you sell a Lee County house?
sections.html:
The exemption does not travel with the house. A buyer has to apply for their own, and the prior owner's benefit comes off the roll the next January 1.

The appraiser warns that a TRIM notice showing homestead in the year of purchase reflects the seller's benefit, which will be removed. Sellers should also know that renting the property long term, or changing how title is held (certain trusts or LLCs), can end the exemption, and the office asks to be contacted when ownership changes in any manner.

If you move to another Florida home, homestead and the Save Our Homes portability benefit must be applied for again at the new address. Florida's state portability rule gives a three-year window counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up, and the form is DR-501T filed by March 1.

sections.h2: What is the difference between a TRIM notice and the tax bill in Lee County?
sections.html:
The TRIM notice is a proposal mailed by the appraiser in mid-August; the tax bill is the actual charge mailed by the Tax Collector, usually in November. Only the bill contains non-ad valorem assessments such as garbage, fire or water charges.

The notice lists market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed taxes. State rules give 25 days from the notice to petition the Value Adjustment Board on value, filed with the clerk. A denied exemption has its own 30-day window after the denial letter is mailed. Read both documents when you list a house, because buyers will ask what the taxes were.

The Tax Collector's office says Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027 and does not change the 2026 bill. Rates for individual taxing authorities and school, city and district millage vary by address, so use the parcel lookup on the appraiser's site and the proposed-tax figures on your own notice rather than a county-wide average.

sections.h2: How is Lee County property tax handled when you sell?
sections.html:
The closing agent splits the year's tax between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. The Tax Collector sends the full-year bill to whoever is the owner of record when the roll arrives, so a seller can still receive one after closing.

The Tax Collector's advice is to forward such a bill to the new owner or to the closing agent. Because a change of ownership is recorded with the clerk and then passed to the appraiser, a gap of weeks is normal. Unpaid delinquent tax shows up as a lien in the title search and is paid from the seller's proceeds at closing.

Florida deed document stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, so Lee County is at the standard rate. All parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay, and the clerk collects it at recording.

sections.h2: What does Lee County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lee County is a Gulf Coast county of about 875,607 people (Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025), up 15.1 percent from the April 2020 base, spread over 781 square miles of land.

The Census Bureau reports 479,540 housing units, a 74.3 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $362,200 and median household income of $76,107 for 2020 to 2024. Residents 65 and over make up 29.2 percent of the population, which is one reason the senior exemptions above matter in sales. The county's municipalities named by the appraiser are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach, and most owners outside those limits sit in unincorporated areas billed by the same offices.

faqs.q: Is Lee County property tax due every year on the same dates?
faqs.a: Yes. Bills become payable November 1 and are due by March 31, and unpaid balances turn delinquent April 1. The early discount scale of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent runs November through February.

faqs.q: Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?
faqs.a: No. Applications must reach the Tax Collector by April 30 of the tax year, and the window opens each November 1. After that, the partial payment plan (through March 31) is the main alternative for current-year tax.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files their own application, and the appraiser removes the prior owner's homestead the following January 1. A TRIM notice showing homestead after a purchase does not mean the buyer qualified.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a wrong value on my Lee County notice?
faqs.a: Call the Property Appraiser at 239-533-6100 first. For a formal challenge, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, using the DR-486 forms the state names.

faqs.q: What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?
faqs.a: The unpaid amount, plus any delinquency charges, is paid from the sale proceeds at closing through the title company. Delinquent real estate tax cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck, so arrange certified funds with the Tax Collector's office.
